QuestionText: A figure with line symmetry can be folded to give two identical halves
Options: C) Only if it is a rectangle
Explanation: Line symmetry: folding along axis gives two identical mirror-image halves.

QuestionText: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
Explanation: 4 lines: 2 through midpoints of opposite sides, 2 through opposite corners.

QuestionText: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
Explanation: 3 lines: one through each vertex to the midpoint of opposite side.

QuestionText: The letter H has ___ line(s) of symmetry
Explanation: H has both a horizontal and vertical line of symmetry: 2 lines.

QuestionText: Rotational symmetry means the figure maps onto itself after a partial rotation
Explanation: Rotational symmetry: figure looks same after rotation by angle < 360 degrees.

QuestionText: Order of rotational symmetry of a square
Explanation: Square: same at 90, 180, 270, 360 degrees: order 4.

QuestionText: Order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle
Explanation: Equilateral triangle: same at 120, 240, 360: order 3.

QuestionText: Angle of rotation for figure with rotational symmetry of order 6
Explanation: 360/6=60 degrees.

QuestionText: The number of lines of symmetry of a circle is
Explanation: Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry: infinite lines.

QuestionText: Regular pentagon has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: Regular n-gon has n lines of symmetry. Pentagon: 5.

QuestionText: Scalene triangle has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: No equal sides or angles: no line of symmetry.

QuestionText: Isosceles triangle has ___ line(s) of symmetry
Explanation: 1 line: perpendicular bisector of the base.

QuestionText: Rectangle (non-square) has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: 2 lines through midpoints of opposite sides.

QuestionText: Kite has ___ line of symmetry
Explanation: 1 line along main diagonal.

QuestionText: Angle of rotational symmetry of order 4
Explanation: 360/4=90 degrees.

QuestionText: Regular hexagon has ___ lines of symmetry and rotational order ___
Explanation: Regular hexagon: 6 lines, order 6 (every 60 degrees).

QuestionText: Rhombus (non-square) has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: 2 lines along diagonals.

QuestionText: Parallelogram (non-rectangle) has ___ line symmetry
Explanation: Parallelogram has NO line symmetry but has rotational order 2.

QuestionText: Which shape has both 4 lines of symmetry and rotational order 4?
Explanation: Square: 4 lines of symmetry AND rotational order 4.

QuestionText: Regular octagon has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: Regular n-gon has n lines of symmetry. Octagon: 8.

QuestionText: Letter A has ___ line of symmetry
Explanation: A has 1 vertical line of symmetry.

QuestionText: Letter S has rotational symmetry of order
Explanation: S maps onto itself after 180 degree rotation: order 2.

QuestionText: Letter X has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: X has horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry: 2.

QuestionText: The letter N has ___ line symmetry but rotational order ___
Explanation: N has no line symmetry but order 2 rotational symmetry.

QuestionText: If a figure has n-fold rotational symmetry it maps onto itself every ___ degrees
Explanation: Angle of rotation = 360/n.

QuestionText: A circle has rotational symmetry of infinite order because ___
Options: A) Any rotation maps it onto itself
D) Only 360 maps it to itself
Explanation: A circle maps onto itself for any angle of rotation.

QuestionText: A regular 10-sided polygon has order of rotational symmetry
Explanation: Regular n-gon: order = n = 10.

QuestionText: Folding along line of symmetry creates two ___ halves
Explanation: Folding creates mirror-image halves.

QuestionText: The number 8 has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: Digit 8 has both horizontal and vertical line symmetry: 2 lines.

QuestionText: A regular star with 5 points has ___ lines of symmetry
Explanation: 5-pointed star has 5 lines of symmetry.

QuestionText: Isosceles trapezium has ___ line of symmetry
Explanation: 1 line: perpendicular bisector of the two parallel sides.

QuestionText: Which word has a vertical line of symmetry (capital letters)?
Explanation: M, O, M are all vertically symmetric letters. MOM has a vertical line of symmetry.

QuestionText: A dart (arrowhead) kite has ___ line of symmetry
Explanation: 1 line: along the axis of the dart.

QuestionText: Minimum order of rotational symmetry any figure has
Explanation: Order 1 means only a full 360 degree rotation maps it to itself.

QuestionText: A regular 12-sided polygon has order of rotational symmetry
Explanation: Regular 12-gon: order 12.

QuestionText: A scalene triangle has rotational symmetry of order
Explanation: No symmetry below 360 degrees: order 1.

QuestionText: Order of rotational symmetry of the letter Z
Explanation: Z maps onto itself after 180 degrees: order 2.

QuestionText: Which figure has both line symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 2 but NOT 4?
Explanation: Rectangle: 2 lines of symmetry, rotational order 2. Not 4.

QuestionText: Axis of symmetry of a parabola y=x squared is
Explanation: y=x² is symmetric about the y-axis.

QuestionText: Fold a square along diagonal. The two halves are
Explanation: Diagonal fold of a square gives two congruent right isosceles triangles.

QuestionText: Circle inscribed in a square: lines of symmetry of the combined figure
Explanation: The combined figure has the symmetry of the square (4 lines) since the square is more restrictive.

QuestionText: If a figure looks the same after every 45 degree rotation its order of rotational symmetry is
Regular hexagon: total degrees covered by all minimal rotations (excluding 360)
Explanation: 60+120+180+240+300=900. Hmm: let's say excluding 360, order 6 gives 60,120,180,240,300 degrees. Sum=900.

QuestionText: A figure with rotational symmetry of order 5 maps onto itself at every ___ degrees
Explanation: 360/5=72 degrees.

QuestionText: In a reflection the line of symmetry is the ___ bisector of any point and its image
Explanation: The line of symmetry is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining any point to its reflected image.

QuestionText: A figure that has both horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry also has rotational symmetry of order
Explanation: Two perpendicular lines of symmetry imply at least order 2 rotational symmetry (180 degree rotation).

QuestionText: Semi-circle has ___ line of symmetry
Explanation: Semicircle has 1 line of symmetry: the perpendicular bisector of the diameter.

QuestionText: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
Explanation: F has no line of symmetry. A, H, M all have at least one.

QuestionText: Letters with horizontal line of symmetry include
Explanation: B, D, E have horizontal lines of symmetry.

QuestionText: Regular polygon with 180 sides has order of rotational symmetry
Explanation: Regular n-gon: order = n = 180.
